title: Pacific: islands over centuries
hook: Was Pacific settlement one continuous expedition?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Scrubbing the dates reveals a long pause, not one unbroken expedition.

claims.text: c. 1300 BCE: Near Oceania. Lapita communities live in the Bismarck islands.
claims.source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/pacific-migrations/print — Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand

claims.text: 1100–800 BCE: West Polynesia. Settlement reaches Fiji, Tonga and Samoa.
claims.source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/pacific-migrations/print — Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand

claims.text: After 1000 CE: East Polynesia. Voyagers settle eastern archipelagos.
claims.source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/pacific-migrations/print — Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand

claims.text: c. 1300 CE: Aotearoa. Polynesian settlers reach Aotearoa New Zealand.
claims.source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/pacific-migrations/print — Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand

claims.text: Scrubbing the dates reveals a long pause, not one unbroken expedition. Settlement spread into West Polynesia in the second millennium BCE; eastern archipelagos were settled much later. Aotearoa was reached around 1300 CE. These were generations of skilled navigation and settlement.
claims.source: https://teara.govt.nz/en/pacific-migrations/print — Geoff Irwin: Remote Oceania, settlement sequence and New Zealand
